results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 75 aligned outline summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in spec order (p01-p74); the five opening callouts are not spec paragraphs and match nothing.

p03 (Introduction ¶3), marked two_ideas by the outliner: The spec's controlling idea joins the two terms and the Veldmark group they are applied to; the paragraph does both. The Keybridge sentence is a scope note on 'three listing brands' (recorded under flow), not a second controlling idea.
p11 (Concepts ¶4), marked two_ideas by the outliner: Comparative use and filling with numbers are one idea: numbers make the comparison checkable, as the spec states.
p42 (Architecture ¶13), marked two_ideas by the outliner: The two design rules are announced as one idea ('Two design rules keep the seams honest'), matching the spec.

p43 (Worked Example ¶1), marked two_ideas by the outliner: The spec's controlling idea itself pairs the answer preview with the spring check against three listings; the paragraph frames the section. The chronology problem it causes is recorded under flow_is_followable.
p48 (Worked Example ¶6), marked two_ideas by the outliner: 'Two consequences follow' introduces one idea, how Table 7 must be read against the profile (volume versus value), as the spec states.
p49 (Worked Example ¶7), marked two_ideas by the outliner: The two bullets serve one idea: the profile decides the layer per section of Tradeyard Poland.

Every body paragraph ties to a supporting claim through its section: scene and differ to V1; concepts and in-practice to V1/V2 (Kleinanzeigen p29 to V2 at feature level); who-decides to V1/V5; architecture p30-p42 to V2/V3/V4; trade-offs to V2/V5; worked example to V1/V2/V4/V5; failure modes to V3/V5; Chief Architect and questions to V2-V5. No orphan paragraph.

Tables 1-8 each have a caption or adjacent sentence stating what they show (Table 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 captions state the result; Table 1 and 3 captions plus p09/p57 state the grouping and the outside-party point; p45, p48, p52 read Tables 6-8). Figures 1-4 have explanatory captions and in-text readings (p18, p30/p38, p41, p45). Quotations (Felix, AVIV, Adevinta, Vinted, the real-estate model, Rightmove, InfoJobs, Google, Indeed, Kleinanzeigen) are each followed by what they show. Clarity problems with individual examples are recorded under flow_is_followable.

results.quote: Felix's gate guards against one way option B decays; this is the first of six.
results.finding: The boundary into Failure Modes should elaborate from Felix's stage gate and option B's decay to six recurring decay modes. The sentence picks up both, but 'this' is ambiguous (the gate or the bolded failure) and the gate was presented as the defence against the Forced Fit, not against B decaying, so the relationship is asserted rather than made visible; both flow readers had to re-read it.

All other boundaries (introduction p02-p04, every section's transition_in and every paragraph transition_in through p74) express the declared relationship and pick up the declared known information, e.g. 'To turn Ingrid's answers into profiles' (concepts), 'The row sections above cited the record one dimension at a time' (in-practice), 'Verticals differ, outside parties rewrite their requirements and sharing decisions get reversed, so' (architecture), 'The four layers are one answer; a group could choose others' (trade-offs), 'Each of these failures starts as an undecided or unwatched question' (Chief Architect), 'This chapter opened with the synergy case's question' (conclusion).

Post level: both flow readers state the organising principle as problem, tools, evidence, design, choice, application, governance, which agrees with the declared prerequisite_order (with assertion_evidence_reasoning for differ to architecture). No section is marked unclear by either reader (Who Decides is 'only partly clear' for A and 'mostly clear' for B; neither lost the thread there). Points not counted as material: the failure-pattern names Ghost Inventory, Seeing Double and Deal-Shaped Architecture (both readers) are on the audience's already_knows list; Figure 3's 'eight vertical seams' (both readers) depends on the image the readers did not see; 'three rows' asserted before support (both readers call it minor and say the subsections justify it).

results.quote: Veldmark's workshop applies the profile and the share test; its answer, Table 8 below, is option B with D for two vertical capabilities. The workshop drafts its profiles from recent listings. Over the spring, Ingrid's team checks them against three listings this book follows through Parts II and III (Table 6).
results.finding: Both readers lost the thread on the worked example's chronology: the answer is given first, then spring listings (Golf 14 April, Lyon May), then the March draft and April ratification, and the scene's 'one real listing' per brand does not match the three tracked listings. A: 'The timeline is tangled... I had to piece the sequence together myself. Giving the answer (Table 8) before the evidence also makes the order of the section feel inverted.' The answer-first opening and the listings-before-classification order are declared in the spec (p43 controlling idea, section transition_in, small_to_large flow), and both readers propose reordering, so the order itself causes the difficulty.
results.corroborated_by: second flow reader (B), item 3a ('This was the main place I lost the thread')

Terms on does_not_know are given at or before first substantive use: VIN as a 17-character vehicle identity decoded into manufacturer data (intro ¶2, p17), type-approval codes hsn/tsn (p17), DMS (scene ¶2), MLS and ATS (Table 2), IDX (Table 3), DPE (p24), ESCO and O*NET (p17); the profile and share test are defined in Concepts before use. Failure-pattern names (Ghost Inventory, Seeing Double, Deal-Shaped Architecture) are on already_knows. Paragraph openings start from introduced material.

The introduction opens with Part I's sameness and the synergy case's question ('Can it?'), states the physics thesis with four concrete items, defines the two owned terms and gives a roadmap; none of the five weak patterns.

The conclusion opens by returning to the opening question, does not start with 'in conclusion', adds no new subtopic, holds no body evidence beyond the Veldmark outcome already shown, and ends on a takeaway and a hand-off, not a restated thesis alone.

p72 states what no single section states (no for one listing model, yes for the machinery beneath, as the last step of Part I's reasoning ending in the share test); p73 gives the so-what (a ratified table instead of argument, a stage gate on Motorvane's own metrics) and the course of action.

p72 returns to the opening question verbatim in substance ('can one listing platform, with a category tree per vertical, carry a used sofa, a family car, an apartment and a job?') and p73 to Part I's claim that the business decides the architecture, as callback.to requires.

The cold reader predicted, in order, the workshop scene, the two definitions, the five-vertical comparison, the public record, the outside parties, the four-layer platform, the trade-off against pure strategies, three Veldmark listings plus the workshop's classification, failure modes, the Chief Architect's view and review questions, with evidence from numbers, public cases and fictional Veldmark; this matches the expected answer.

The reader says the plan should not decide; the move happens when the shared ingestion engine meets the car vertical's profile (dealer-feed requirements), measured by the brand's feed success rate and delete latency, as a stage gate; dealer-feed adapters and the vehicle schema are layer-2 vertical content; vehicle identity, specification decoding and price rating is a layer-3 capability owned by the car brand. Matches the expected answer.
